text:
maria_r: Hey runtime — can someone take a quick look at PR #2250? It's an adaptive-evict heuristic for the quantized batcher that changes default `cache_ttl` from 60s -> 6s for q4_* variants. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2250

alex.h: Looking now. did you run microbench for 2k-10k seqs? last time we saw p95 blow up once cache hit ratio < 0.6.

sam: fyi we should add a perf-smoke that simulates bursty short requests. helps verify batching benefits + opt-out flag for Dedicated pools.

maria_r: I ran a quick sweep — pasted numbers in the PR description:
- q4_0, 2k seq: p95 = 82ms -> 98ms after change
- cost/token down ~14% in avg throughput tests
But I don't have long-tail traces yet. CI is green but perf-smoke flagged as flaky in one job.

ci-bot: CI: build=passed, unit_tests=1243 passed, perf-smoke=flaky (job #982). Full logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/982

jay: If perf-smoke is flaky we should pause prod canary. Can infra schedule a small canary (2 GPU) in us-west2 to validate real traffic?

ops-oncall: ops-oncall: can do. earliest slot Tue 09:00 PT. Please tag me when you start the canary run.

irene: minor note — routing policy needs a fallback tweak. when cache miss cascade happens we should reroute to compat model (q8 variant) to avoid tail latency spikes.

alex.h: Also add a short benchmark for long sequences (8k+ tokens) — if kv-cache eviction changes then mem pressure + kernel selection interact and can cause latency regressions.

maria_r: Good calls. I'll: 1) add perf bench for 2k/8k workloads, 2) add opt-out flag for Dedicated pools, 3) update routing fallback to include q8 variants, and 4) re-run smoke in CI. Aiming to request merge Thu AM.

sam: Thanks — ping @eng-runtime for a perf approval when benches land. :thumbsup:

maria_r: will do. tagging here for visibility so infra/oncall can plan canary. Appreciate quick eyes!
